classification.difficultyReason: Expand the transformed-root product and organise its terms into the root sum, pair-product sum and product before substituting the cubic coefficient relationships.

content.prompt:
Find the value of
$$(2\alpha-1)(2\beta-1)(2\gamma-1)$$
if $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are the roots of $x^3-4x+2=0$.

answer.short:
$-1$

Expand the product and substitute the cubic root-coefficient relationships.
answer.worked:
By the cubic root-coefficient relationships,
$$\begin{align*}
\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=0\\
\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma&=-4\\
\alpha\beta\gamma&=-2.
\end{align*}$$
Expand the product:
$$\begin{align*}
(2\alpha-1)(2\beta-1)(2\gamma-1)&=8\alpha\beta\gamma-4(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma)+2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)-1\\
(2\alpha-1)(2\beta-1)(2\gamma-1)&=8(-2)-4(-4)+2(0)-1\\
(2\alpha-1)(2\beta-1)(2\gamma-1)&=-1.
\end{align*}$$
